```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mizer)
library(mizerShelf)
params <- validParams(NWMed_params)
```

mizerShelf adds a dynamic detritus spectrum and a scalar carrion biomass.
Detritus uses the resource state; carrion is a registered component that adds
`rho * carrion_biomass` to consumer encounter rates. The extension class records
its package version and enables upgrading saved models. Ordinary mizer methods
now use the capabilities stored in the model for projection, measurements,
settling, tuning and structural changes.

## Equations and stepping

Both budgets have the form

\[
\frac{dB}{dt} = P - c B.
\]

Carrion production includes external consumer mortality, excess gear mortality
and discards. Its losses include consumption and decomposition. Detritus inputs
include unassimilated food, decomposing carrion and a signed external inflow;
consumers remove detritus. Detritus preserves its current spectrum shape while
changing total biomass. Its equations require positive biomass: the model does
not invent a spectrum shape at an empty stock. New models start with zero
decomposition and external detritus inflow, and an external-mortality carrion
fraction of one; calibration then sets the two budget parameters.

The component and resource declarations supply exact equations separately from
their exponential step functions. Those steps handle fast losses without
claiming a higher coupled integration order. Every callback receives the complete
effective rate list, including fishing mortality. No selective getter fallback
reconstructs missing rates.

## Measurements and plots

Biomass measurement is separate from convergence assessment. Carrion declares
one biomass series, and mizer integrates the resource over the full size grid.
The default getter returns consumer species, consistently with other mizer
models. Select extra measurements explicitly:

```{r biomass}
b <- getBiomass(params, include = c("species", "resource", "component:carrion"))
names(b)
```

The stable IDs of the extra series are `resource` and
`component:carrion/biomass`. Their labels and styles travel with the measurement.
`plotBiomass(params, include = ...)` follows the same measurement-and-plot path.
Carrion is unstructured, so it does not advertise size or length filters; an
explicit unsupported filter produces an unavailable measurement with a reason.

`plotDeath()` delegates to the checked mortality diagnostic. For a simulation,
it retains mizerShelf's established final-state meaning. The cause list is
checked against the actual total mortality, rather than adding a cause that the
dynamical equations do not use.

The shipped `NWMed_params` has historically used `mizerMort`, although carrion
production counts gear kills. This scientific discrepancy is preserved during
upgrading. New constructor models use `seMort`, and their decomposition includes
excess gear mortality. Changing the shipped mortality law would be a separate
model change, not a migration.

## Settling and tuning

Whole-model convergence assesses consumers, detritus and carrion separately.
The two shelf measures report biomass rates and tolerances in grams per year.
`findSteadyState(solver = "project")` and `projectUntilSettled()` evolve the
components and assess those equations without changing parameters.

`tuneSteadyState()` uses the stored `shelf_budgets` joint strategy. It holds both
shelf states fixed while consumers settle, then adjusts only the carrion
`decompose` coefficient and detritus `external` inflow. The target constructor
records separate source and loss fluxes. The balancer solves those budgets
analytically, and mizer independently verifies the targets, unchanged state,
allowed parameter paths and every effective consumer equation rate. The final
whole-model assessment uses the restored physical equations.

Negative decomposition is infeasible and produces an error. No generic
numerical fallback or consumer repair follows a failed balance.
`tune_carrion_detritus()` remains an explicit helper for balancing just the two
budgets at the supplied state, with independent rate and state checks. It is
restricted to the known Shelf provider family with carrion as its only component.
For composed or modified models, use `tuneSteadyState()` with declared coordinated
strategies so mizer verifies every affected owner's equations.

`rr_pp` and `cc_pp` do not appear in the detritus budget. The former no-op
`balance_detritus_dynamics()` has been removed. Use
`setResource(..., balance = FALSE)` for resource parameter edits, then invoke
budget calibration explicitly when appropriate.

## Species, grids and units

Declared transformation hooks run after core dimension bookkeeping and before
any rate construction or initial-state evaluation. They resize and rename
`rho` using explicit species/grid maps and preserve old overlapping values.
There is no late repair after `addSpecies()` or `removeSpecies()`.

For added species, provide `rho_carrion` to specify carrion encounter. Missing
values now default to zero, with an explanatory message; they are no longer
inferred by a late feeding-level calculation. `steady = FALSE` performs only the
structural operation. `steady = TRUE` selects mizer's normal new-species steady
initialisation. The constructor still derives its initial `rho_carrion` from
feeding level and encounter when building a new model.

The same declarations cover species reordering, renaming, removal, grid changes,
abundance scaling and rate scaling. They update `rho`, its scalar coefficients,
component biomass and budget parameters according to their units. Missing
required extension support is an error before the original model is changed.

## Scope of stability analysis

The stored declarations distinguish autonomous dynamics from prescribed inputs.
Carrion is dynamic even when its rate happens to be zero. The current mizer
Jacobian does not include dynamic component coordinates, so whole-model stability
is reported as incomplete. An explicitly conditional analysis may hold carrion
fixed; the result records that restriction. Genuine zero modes in the detritus
shape are retained rather than being inferred to be prescribed coordinates.
